s.n: Office party beef and onion sausage rolls
s.note: the catering table at the office party
s.how: Fry 2 sliced onions in 20g butter for 15 minutes until golden, then cool. Mix 300g beef mince and 200g pork mince with the onions, 1 tsp thyme, 40g breadcrumbs, 1 egg and salt. Cut 2 sheets puff pastry in half, lay a log of filling along each, roll and seal. Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with sesame and cut each into 4. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with 200g tomato relish.

s.note: Clay throwing one party to save the branch
s.how: Unwrap a 250g camembert, sit it back in its wooden box or a small dish and cut slits in the top. Push in slivers of 1 garlic clove and small rosemary sprigs and drizzle with 1 tbsp honey. Bake at 180C for 15 minutes until soft in the middle. Slice 1 baguette, brush with oil and toast 8 minutes. Serve the cheese hot on a board with the toasts, 300g grapes and 4 tbsp fig jam.

m.note: the Zenotek branch party that gets out of control
m.how: Slowly fry 2 sliced onions in 20g butter for 15 minutes. Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp mustard and 1 tbsp chopped pickles. Roll 600g beef mince into 12 balls, smash flat in a very hot oiled pan, season and cook 2 minutes. Flip, add half a cheese slice each and cook 1 minute. Toast 12 brioche slider buns and fill with sauce, patty, onions and pickles.

w.how: Beat 125g butter and 150g sugar, add 2 eggs, 200g self-raising flour and 120ml milk. Bake 12 cupcakes at 180C for 18 minutes. Beat 150g butter with 300g icing sugar, tint half red and half green and pipe on.

d.note: the CEO sister out to close the branch
d.how: Whisk 4 egg yolks with 100g caster sugar. Heat 600ml milk, 200ml cream, 1 cinnamon stick and 1 tsp vanilla until steaming. Slowly whisk into the yolks, then return to the pan and stir over low heat until it coats a spoon, about 5 minutes. Strain and chill 2 hours. Stir in 60ml dark rum and 60ml brandy, or serve those on the side. Pour into glasses and grate fresh nutmeg over the top.
